question.text: Aranya Cat III AIF has the following at quarter-end: Listed equity portfolio (FMV) = INR 85 crore; Unlisted equity (Registered-Valuer FMV) = INR 12 crore; Corporate bonds (amortised cost) = INR 8 crore; Cash = INR 2 crore; Management fee payable = INR 80 lakh; Tax provision = INR 1.20 crore. Units outstanding = 5,00,000. Compute NAV per unit.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Total Assets = 85 + 12 + 8 + 2 = INR 107 crore. Total Liabilities = 0.80 + 1.20 = INR 2 crore. Net Assets = 105 crore = INR 1,05,00,00,000. NAV per unit = 1,05,00,00,000 / 5,00,000 = INR 2,100. Per Section 14.10, NAV = (Total Assets - Total Liabilities) / Units outstanding. **The Trap:** INR 2,140 forgets to deduct tax provision. INR 2,120 deducts only management fee. INR 2,080 double-counts liabilities. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) tests NAV conceptually; XIX-C demands the line-item mechanics — unlisted at Registered-Valuer FMV, bonds at amortised cost when no ascertainable market, per Section 14.10.1. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Insist that the fund accountant segregates 'provisions' (estimated tax, accrued incentive fee) from hard liabilities. Mis-classification inflates NAV and triggers LP disputes when the final tax bill lands lower than provision.
